newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Forbes makes debut in Botswana bourse.
newsitem.headline: Forbes makes debut in Botswana bourse.

text.p: The South African Forbes Group, a professional services organisation, this morning listed 215,145,200 shares on the Botswana Stock Exchange (BSE).
The group is also listed on the Namibian and Johannesburg exchanges. The shares came on the board at 682 thebe and 1,500 changed hands during Friday trading.

"Forbes now has interests in South Africa, Namibia, Botswana, Zambia and Mauritius and associates in Swaziland and Lesotho. We are looking at Angola, Mozambique, Zimbabwe and Kenya," group financial director David Bergman said.

Bergman said the main elements of the group were employee benefits, actuarial consultants Alexander Forbes, which last year contributed 42 percent of the group's 624 million South African rand revenue, risk management and short-term insurance broker Price Forbes, which contributed 54 percent.
Major shareholders were Sanlam with 46.33 percent, management and staff trusts with 19.17 percent. The balance was in the market.
Forbes operations in Botswana cover both short-term insurance broking, employee benefits and actuarial consulting.

Alexander Forbes and Price Forbes have been represented in Botswana since November 1995 when they acquired interests in Time Fund Managers (Proprietary) Limited and Ngamiland Trust (Proprietary) Limited, a registered Botswana broker.

Botswana Development Corporation Corporate Finance and Divestment Division Manager Kumbalani Munamati said Forbes was the fifth foreign company to dual list on the BSE this year and had significantly boosted domestic investment opportunities in Botswana," Munamati said.

"There has been a substantial leap in interest in the BSE from both foreign and local investors. Botswana has outpaced Johannesburg by a wide margin in the central and southern African stock market race this year.

"It has risen 41 percent in US dollar terms in the first five months of 1997, well ahead of Namibia, which has posted 16 percent growth, South Africa and Kenya with 14 percent and Zimbabwe with 10 percent growth."

Munamati said the dual listing policy introduced in Januray was proving a significant boost for the development of the capital market in Botswana and a step towards the development of the country as a financial services centre.
"Botswana has tremendous potential to emerge as the region's Financial Services Centre," he said.
"It is among the fastest growing economies in the world, rated by the Economist Intelligence Unit in 11th spot behind the so-called "Asian Tigers"," he said.
In terms of Institutional Investor Credit Ratings for 1996, Botswana had also performed extremely well, placed 44th in the world rankings and second in Africa.
